pr.title: Expire sessions after a week of inactivity
pr.author: dana

hunks.header: @@ -6,3 +6,11 @@ test("creates and resolves a session", async () => {

guide.overview:
Sessions now expire after seven days without activity. The change adds `expiresAt` to the session model, enforces it in `SessionManager.resolve`, slides it forward on each authenticated request, and mirrors it in the cookie.

The risk is in `resolve`: the expired-session delete is not awaited, and sessions stored before this change have no `expiresAt`.

steps.title: Sessions gain an expiry
steps.narrative: `Session` now carries `expiresAt`, and a seven-day `DEFAULT_TTL_MS` is introduced. Every later step reads or writes this field, so check that it is required rather than optional: existing stored sessions will not have it.

steps.title: The manager sets, checks and extends expiry
steps.narrative: `create` stamps `expiresAt`, `resolve` rejects and deletes expired sessions, and the new `touch` slides the expiry forward. The clock is injectable so tests can move time. This is where the behavior change lives: look at the expired branch in `resolve` closely.

steps.title: HTTP layer: cookie expiry and sliding sessions
steps.narrative: Login now sets the cookie's `expires` to match the session, and the middleware calls `touch` on every authenticated request and clears the cookie on a 401.

steps.title: Tests and docs
steps.narrative: One new test covers expiry with a fake clock. Nothing covers `touch` or the middleware yet.

steps.title: Lockfile
steps.narrative: An empty `packages` map added by npm. Safe to skim.

annotations.body: Injecting the clock is what lets the new test move time forward without sleeping.

comments.body: The delete is not awaited, so a store error becomes an unhandled rejection and the request still returns as if the session was cleaned up. Await it (or deliberately `void` it and catch).
Sessions written before this deploy have no `expiresAt`. `undefined < date` is `false`, so they never expire. Either backfill the store or treat a missing `expiresAt` as `createdAt + ttl`.
`touch` writes to the store on every authenticated request. Consider only extending when less than half the TTL remains.
Should this also set `secure: true`? We only serve over HTTPS.
Good call, I'll add it in a follow-up so this PR stays about expiry.
Can we add a test for `touch` sliding the expiry, and one for the middleware clearing the cookie?
